core.title: Interlocking routes go through the interlocking runner, and every route ends in the train runner
core.given: The composition root (the station master) has a journey map that declares at least one interlocking route object (a route of the form {interlockingId, path})
core.when: you write or change the composition root
core.then: The composition root MUST resolve each interlocking route through the interlocking runner, and the train runner MUST perform the final train execution for every route: both the train the interlocking runner selects and each directly named train id.
prefer: Delegation chain: the composition root asks the interlocking runner to resolve the action to a selected train (with the action's inputs and the current state) and hands the selected train id to the train runner for execution
Use the runner API that actually exists in this stack rather than copying a call model or a fix hint verbatim
avoid: Declaring an interlocking route without routing it through the interlocking runner
Never reaching the train runner for the interlocking-selected train
Executing directly named train-id routes through any executor other than the train runner
unless: The journey map declares no interlocking route object: a purely direct-train composition root carries no interlocking obligation
core.why: In both cases, direct and interlocking, the train runner performs the final train execution. A composition root that declares an interlocking route but never routes through the interlocking runner, or never reaches the train runner, breaks the contract.
evidence: The stack's check for this obligation reports no finding for the composition root: neither an unlinked interlocking route nor missing delegation to the train runner
The composition root references the interlocking runner and the train runner whenever the journey map holds an interlocking route object
Both directly named train-id entries and interlocking-selected trains reach the train runner for final execution
verification: The check scans the composition root and triggers only when the journey map declares at least one interlocking route object; activation depends only on that presence, not on other detector findings, and the check does not fire for a purely direct-train composition root or for files outside the composition root

When triggered, a missing reference to the interlocking runner is reported as an unlinked interlocking route, and a missing reference to the train runner as missing delegation; the concrete finding identifiers are the realization's
Which entrypoint is inspected, and how the journey map, its route forms and the runner references are recognized, is up to the per-stack detector

Disposition strict, severity 4: an unlinked or non-delegating composition root cannot be suppressed and fails CI — a failing check run must fail the continuous-integration build, not merely report the finding

The automated check verifies only that the train-runner reference is present; that directly named train-id entries are actually executed by the train runner must be confirmed by reviewing the dispatch

values: the journey map of the composition root contains at least one interlocking route object {interlockingId, path}

fires: A task adds an interlocking route object to the composition root's journey map
An agent edits a composition root whose journey map already holds interlocking route objects, including its direct-route dispatch
The composition root declares an interlocking route but does not reference the interlocking runner or the train runner
doesNotFire: The journey map holds only directly named train-id entries
Files other than the composition root

neutralityNotes: Station master, journey map, interlocking route object {interlockingId, path}, interlocking runner, train runner and train id are the ATDD runtime's shared domain vocabulary (the agnostic core obligation coder.train.station-master-interlocking-routing, core runtime spec afokapu/atdd#1251), so they remain in the core; only their concrete identifiers (server.ts, the JOURNEY_MAP export, the InterlockingRunner/TrainRunner classes and their resolveTrain/execute signatures, the ./trains/* import paths, checks/interlocking_station_routing.mjs, and the finding ids 'unlinked'/'no delegation') are Bun and live in bunOnly. CI failure is treated as stack-neutral enforcement (every stack's convention checks gate its continuous-integration build) and is kept in core:verification; only the shared:policy.strict-disposition cross-reference pointer stays with the realization. Stack scoping (the doesNotFire entry 'Non-Bun stacks' and the atdd.workspace.bun detector-family applicability note) stays with each realization, since a stack-neutral core carries no stack identity. The {interlockingId, path} route-object shape is kept verbatim as the runtime-level route form shared across stacks; a stack that realizes the route object differently owns its concrete syntax while the core keeps the two-form distinction (directly named train id vs interlocking route object). How the journey map, route forms and runner references are recognized is deliberately deferred to the per-stack detector (core:verification), as the Bun text itself does, so no profile key was proposed for recognition.
